extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, petitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and other parties practicing before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board in AIA trials (IPR, PGR, CBM, derivation)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and practice guidance for conducting inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, and derivation proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board under the AIA, including claim construction, motions to amend, discovery limits, briefing limits, certifications, and institution standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard — broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in an unexpired patent that will not expire before a final written decision shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification of the patent in which it appears. (See proposed amendments to 37 CFR 42.100(b), 42.200(b), and 42.300(b).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will continue to apply BRI to claims in unexpired patents in AIA proceedings, consistent with Federal Circuit precedent (In re Cuozzo). The preamble explains the policy rationale: longstanding PTO practice, public interest in avoiding claims broader than justified, and the availability (however cabined) of amendment in AIA proceedings as justification for BRI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard — Phillips when patent will expire before final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents that will expire prior to issuance of a final written decision by the Office, the Office proposes to apply a Phillips-type standard during the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such patents essentially lack viable opportunity to amend claims in an AIA proceeding; parties may be able to determine before filing which construction will apply. The Office invites comments on procedures (e.g., whether petitioners must brief both standards or whether briefing after filing but before patent owner preliminary response should be entertained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard for inter partes review (IPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes review shall not be instituted for a ground of unpatentability unless the Board decides that the petition supporting the ground would demonstrate that there is a reasonable likelihood that at least one of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable. (§ 42.108(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding institution, the Board will take into account a patent owner preliminary response where filed, but supporting evidence concerning disputed material facts will be viewed in the light most favorable to the petitioner. If patent owner submits supporting evidence, petitioner may seek leave to file a reply under § 42.24(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard for post-grant review (PGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review shall not be instituted for a ground of unpatentability unless the Board decides that the petition supporting the ground would, if unrebutted, demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable. (§ 42.208(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like IPR, the Board will consider a patent owner preliminary response but will view supporting evidence concerning disputed material facts in the light most favorable to the petitioner when deciding whether to institute. Petitioner may seek leave to reply if patent owner files evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response to the petition setting forth the reasons why no IPR or PGR should be instituted and can include supporting evidence. The preliminary response is subject to the word count under § 42.24. (§§ 42.107(a), 42.207(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response evidence will be considered in institution decisions, but disputed material facts' supporting evidence will be viewed in the light most favorable to the petitioner. If patent owner submits supporting evidence, petitioner may seek leave to reply under § 42.24(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend — statutory and substantive limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend may cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims, and by statute must not enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new matter; the Rules include a rebuttable presumption that only one substitute claim is needed to replace each challenged claim. (37 CFR 42.221(a)(3); discussion of 35 U.S.C. 316(d)/326(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners are encouraged to submit a single substitute claim per cancelled claim for efficiency, but may propose more if need shown. Motions to amend cannot be entered like prosecution amendments; the Board does not perform a prior art search for amendments. The Office requires motions to show written description support and that substitute claims are narrower than replaced claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of persuasion and burden of production for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate burden of persuasion to demonstrate patentability of substitute claims remains with the patent owner (movant). Once the patent owner sets forth a prima facie case of patentability of the substitute claims over the prior art of record, the burden of production shifts to the petitioner to rebut. (MasterImage, Microsoft citations; discussion)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must argue patentability over 'prior art of record' (clarified to include prosecution history, material art of record in current or other Office proceedings) and 'prior art known to the patent owner' (material prior art made of record pursuant to duty of candor). Petitioner may rebut by addressing patent owner evidence or identifying additional prior art; patent owner may reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'prior art of record' and 'prior art known to the patent owner' for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'prior art of record' refers to: (a) any material art in the prosecution history of the patent; (b) any material art of record in the current proceeding, including art asserted in grounds on which the Board did not institute review; and (c) any material art of record in any other proceeding before the Office involving the patent. 'Prior art known to the patent owner' means material prior art that Patent Owner makes of record in the current proceeding pursuant to its duty of candor. (MasterImage clarification)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners must address these categories when making their prima facie case for substitute claim patentability; failure to make these showings can allow petitioner to shift burden of production back to challenge patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and procedure for filing motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner's motion to amend must be filed no later than the filing of the patent owner response (and the patent owner must hold a conference call with the Office before filing a motion to amend per 37 CFR 42.121(a) and 42.122(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the motion with the patent owner response is efficient due to the one-year statutory deadline for AIA proceedings. Patent owner may file earlier. During the required pre-filing conference call, judges provide technical guidance regarding the motion; parties should seek authorization from the Board to revise motions if defects are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and word limits for petitions, motions, responses, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Type-volume and page limits are prescribed: e.g., Petition requesting IPR: 14,000 words; PGR petition: 18,700 words; CBM petition: 18,700 words; derivation petition: 14,000 words; motions (excluding motions to amend): 15 pages; motions to amend: 25 pages; replies to patent owner responses: 5,600 words; replies to oppositions (excluding motions to amend): 5 pages; replies to oppositions to motions to amend: 12 pages. (§ 42.24)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word/page counts exclude tables of contents, tables of authorities, certificates of service/word count, exhibits, appendices, and claim listings. Petitions to institute may be accompanied by a motion to waive word counts; such motions must show why waiver is in the interests of justice and append the proposed over-length petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of word counts and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition, preliminary response, patent owner response, or reply subject to type-volume limits must include a certification stating the number of words. Every petition, response, written motion, and other paper must be signed by at least lead counsel or designated backup counsel (or by an unrepresented party). (§§ 42.24(d), 42.11(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may rely on the word count of the word-processing system used. The Board may expunge unsigned submissions unless omission is promptly corrected after being called to attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor; Rule 11-type representations and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting to the Board a petition, response, written motion, or other paper, an attorney, registered practitioner, or unrepresented party certifies that, to the best of the person’s knowledge, information, and belief, formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances: (1) it is not presented for any improper purpose; (2) the claims, defenses, and other legal contentions are warranted by existing law or a non-frivolous argument to change law; (3) factual contentions have evidentiary support; and (4) denials of factual contentions are warranted on the evidence. (§ 42.11(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is coupled with sanctions authority if violations occur; these representations do not apply to disclosures and discovery requests/responses/objections (§ 42.11(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions process, safe-harbor, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board determines § 42.11(c) has been violated, after notice and opportunity to respond, it may impose sanctions on any attorney, registered practitioner, law firm, patent agent, or party responsible. A motion for sanctions must be separate, authorized by the Board under § 42.20, provide written notice to the other party before seeking authorization, and the challenged paper must be withdrawn or corrected within 21 days after service of such notice (or other Board-set time) or the motion must not be filed. The Board may on its own initiative order a show cause. Sanctions must be limited to what suffices to deter repetition and consistent with § 42.12. An order imposing sanctions must describe the sanctioned conduct and explain the basis. (§ 42.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may award reasonable expenses, including attorney’s fees, for a sanctions motion if warranted. Absent exceptional circumstances, a law firm must be held jointly responsible for violations by its partners/associates/employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument demonstrative exhibit timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least seven business days before oral argument and filed no later than the time of the oral argument. (§ 42.70(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing ensures notice and opportunity to review demonstratives before oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year statutory pendency and possible six-month extension
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA proceedings are required by statute to be completed no later than one year from the date on which the Director notices the institution of a review, except where good cause is shown to extend the one-year period, which extension may be no more than six months. (35 U.S.C. 316(a)(11); 37 CFR 42.100(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compressed timeline underpins many procedural choices (e.g., timing of motions to amend, limits on additional exchanges) and counsels efficiency in briefing and discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board will not perform an independent prior art search for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board does not conduct a prior art search to evaluate the patentability of proposed substitute claims; if a motion to amend is granted the substitute claims become part of an issued patent without further examination by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no independent Office examination is performed, the Office sets rules requiring patent owner to make a prima facie case and explains why motions to amend cannot be treated the same as prosecution amendments. That is part of the rationale for requiring patent owners to show patentability and for keeping the ultimate burden of persuasion with the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to cure minor defects in motions to amend (discretionary)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board deems it appropriate, the Board may allow a patent owner to cure minor defects in a motion to amend upon request (e.g., failure to construe a claim term or provide written description support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given time constraints, further exchanges of briefing may be incompatible with the schedule. Patent owners aware of defects should seek authorization from the Board to revise motions as soon as possible. The Board may allow cure but may limit additional briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner estoppel under 37 CFR 42.73(d)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under § 42.73(d)(3), a patent applicant or owner is precluded from taking action inconsistent with an adverse judgment, including obtaining in any patent (1) a claim that is not patentably distinct from a finally refused or canceled claim; or (2) an amendment of a specification or of a drawing that was denied during the trial proceeding, except this provision does not apply to an application or patent that has a different written description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule does not categorically bar obtaining all claims that could have been filed in response to a ground of unpatentability; it bars claims not patentably distinct from finally refused/cancelled claims. Parties may seek a panel conference to cancel claims before final decision; asserting conceded claims in litigation may give rise to sanctions or disciplinary investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to waive word counts — procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to institute may be accompanied by a motion to waive the word counts; the petitioner must show how a waiver of the word counts is in the interests of justice and must append a copy of the proposed petition exceeding the word count to the motion. Any other motion to waive word counts or page limits must be granted in advance of filing. (§ 42.24(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the motion is not granted, the proposed over-length petition may be expunged or returned. Parties should obtain waiver authorization before filing over-length materials.
